gold_rationale: Specific, testable behavior: position is either displayed or it is not. Update rate is handled separately by REQ-002.
Model requirement. Quantified threshold (500 ms) plus explicit operating modes. Use as a positive exemplar in the taxonomy.
Clear capability, directly testable.
Both 'safe' and 'efficient' are undefined. SWEHB names 'efficient' explicitly as a subjective term to avoid. SRS Open Items #1 confirms 'safe route' is unresolved.
Trigger condition and action both stated.
'reasonably close' has no numeric tolerance, so no acceptance criterion can be written. Open Items #2 confirms.
'continuously monitor' specifies no sampling rate or staleness bound. A 1 Hz and a 1000 Hz implementation both satisfy the wording.
Exemplary: quantified threshold tied to a defined quantity (usable fuel capacity).
Threshold and both outputs are unambiguous and testable. Noted as compound only because two obligations share one ID, which affects verification tracking rather than clarity.
The trigger (engine failure) is defined but the required response is not. 'Appropriate corrective action' delegates a flight-safety design decision to the developer.
Testable given a defined sensor range.
Clear capability.
Enumerated list is complete and each field is testable. Compound only in the traceability sense - four display fields under one ID.
Safety-critical inhibit, clearly stated and testable.

'Friendly' is never defined, and SRS Open Items #10 admits friend-or-foe criteria are unresolved, so this safety inhibit can't be implemented or verified as written. Its precedence over REQ-035's pilot override also needs clarification.

'Extremely accurate' has no metric or units. Open Items #7 confirms targeting accuracy is unresolved. Separately, the subject is 'the targeting system', not the SFMC - this may not be a software requirement at all.
Trigger and response both stated. No latency bound, but REQ-021 is where that gap is recorded.
'Clearly indicate' is subjective, and 'greatest danger' implies a threat-ranking function with no stated criteria (closure rate? weapon type? time to impact?).
Mode-triggered action, testable.
Condition and action stated; 'when automatic defense is enabled' is a clear precondition.
Both 'quickly' and 'dangerous' are undefined, and 'respond' does not name an action. Three separate gaps in one sentence.
Clear capability.
Trigger and response stated.
Clear capability.

'Important' is undefined (Open Items #4) and 'securely encrypted' names no algorithm or standard. Also written in passive voice with no subject, so it is unclear the SFMC is the responsible component.
Enumerated scope, testable.
Model requirement: trigger, response, and a 1-second latency bound.
Clear obligation.
Complete enumeration of required fields; each is testable.
'Critical' is undefined (Open Items #3) and 'immediately' has no time bound. It also overlaps REQ-027, which bounds fault display at 1 second, without saying which applies to critical faults.
Testable. Subject is the pilot rather than the SFMC, which is a minor style inconsistency, not a defect.

'Prioritize' names no mechanism (CPU scheduling? function shedding?) and 'nonessential' is undefined. Separately, life-support is NOT listed as an SFMC-connected subsystem in SRS section 1.2, so this requirement references a system the SFMC is not documented to control.
'Seriously damaged' and 'safest destination' are both undefined. Open Items #5 confirms 'safe location' is unresolved.

'Safe location' undefined (Open Items #5). 'Shall be capable of' states a capability rather than a behavior, which is weaker than 'shall fly'. Also overlaps REQ-033 and REQ-005 without stating how they interact.
'Always' is broad, and the SRS doesn't say whether pilot override extends to safety inhibits such as REQ-015's friendly-fire block. Needs clarification; the text alone doesn't prove a contradiction.
Quantified (30 s) and testable. 'Operational' is not formally defined, but boot-to-ready is a reasonable reading.
'Without noticeable delay' is subjective and observer-dependent. Open Items #8 confirms.

The 10 Hz minimum is testable, but 'normal operation' isn't one of the SRS's defined modes and 'flight information' isn't defined, so it's unclear when and to what it applies. It is compatible with REQ-002: both set minimum rates.
Quantified duration, testable.
'Never crash' is a universal negative and cannot be demonstrated by finite testing. Reliability must be expressed statistically or against a defined operational profile.
'Recoverable' is defined only by the fact that recovery is possible, making the requirement circular. No recovery time bound is given either.
'Important mission data' is undefined. Same undefined qualifier as REQ-025, applied to a different subsystem.
'Whenever possible' makes the requirement unfalsifiable - any failure to continue operating can be attributed to it not being possible.
Clear obligation; contents are specified in REQ-045.
Complete enumeration of six event classes, each individually testable. Compound in the traceability sense only.
Clear and testable.
'Sufficient storage' gives no capacity figure and no worst-case event rate to derive one from. Open Items #6 confirms.
Clear precondition on spacecraft operation, testable.
Testable given a defined authorization scheme; REQ-048 provides adjacent context.
'State-of-the-art' names no standard and changes meaning over time, so the same implementation could pass today and fail later. Open Items #9 confirms.
Legitimate design constraint, clearly stated.
Legitimate interface constraint.
Testable, with a clear mode precondition. Subject is maintenance personnel rather than the SFMC - minor style inconsistency only.
Clear obligation with a defined ordering ('before installing').
